observations: Each source question asks for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of integers and binary operators +,-,* without reordering.
The requested quantity is the cardinality of the set of results over all full binary parenthesizations of the operator sequence.
The parameter schema supplies operands and operators with len(operators)=len(operands)-1, matching the fixed sequence structure.
Because only +,-,* are used, all intermediate and final values are integers, so distinct values can be tracked exactly in a set.
The number of full parenthesizations grows Catalan-like, but dynamic programming over contiguous operand intervals avoids enumerating duplicate parenthesizations explicitly.
procedure_plan: Implement solve(parameters): read operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2]. Define DP[i][j] as the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing the subexpression a[i] op[i] ... op[j-1] a[j]. Base case DP[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L from 2 to n, for each i with j=i+L-1, initialize DP[i][j]=empty set. For each split k from i to j-1, combine every x in DP[i][k] with every y in DP[k+1][j] using op[k]: if '+', add x+y; if '-', add x-y; if '*', add x*y. Insert results into DP[i][j]. Return the size of DP[0][n-1]. Use exact integer arithmetic and sets for deduplication.
uncertainty: The plan assumes the source questions' phrase 'inserting parentheses' is equivalent to considering all full binary parenthesizations of the given left-to-right sequence, which is the standard interpretation. If a source intended only some restricted class of parenthesizations, the count could differ, but the supplied statements do not indicate such a restriction.
